clips.title: Lesson 7: Effective prompting techniques (Deep Dive) | AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations Course
clips.why: Anthropic's own course on two habits this lesson builds on: give the model the context and the reason, and show an example.
look: Context means the situation and the purpose, not only the task.
An example of the output you want often says more than a paragraph describing it.
Notice that none of this needs capital letters or threats.
clips.after: Our skills follow the same habits: the goal and its reason first, then signs and a short example, so Nova and people can judge cases the text never names.

clips.title: How to Create Good Agent Skills | Claude Code Guide
clips.why: A quick walk through three best practices from Anthropic's skill guide: be concise, set the degree of freedom, test with different models.
look: Concise: the model is already smart, so only write what it cannot know.
Degrees of freedom: exact commands where there is one safe way, judgement where there are many.
A good and a bad skill side by side.
clips.after: Our verify skill gives exact commands for the first checks and judgement for when to look deeper, which is this idea applied.

clips.title: Stop Writing Bad CLAUDE.md Files
clips.why: Why instructions get ignored, and how pointing to files instead of pasting everything keeps them short enough to be followed.
look: Progressive disclosure for instruction files: a short entry point that points to deeper files.
Why a long file full of rules gets followed less, not more.
Which rules belong in tools and checks instead of in text.
clips.after: That is why our skills link to references/ for depth, keep the body short, and leave the rules that must never break to hooks and required checks.

practice.q: A skill says "NEVER run the whole test suite." Which rewrite will an agent apply best to cases the writer did not imagine?

options.text: "CRITICAL: NEVER, under any circumstances, run the whole test suite."
options.why: Louder, but still no reason. The agent will skip the full suite even on a change to shared code, where it is exactly what is needed.

options.text: "Start with the tests next to your change, because they cover most changes in minutes; run the whole suite when you changed shared code."
options.why: A default, the reason for it, and the sign that says when to go further. The agent can now judge a case the text never named.

options.text: Delete the line and say nothing about tests.
options.why: The habit matters. It needs a reason and a starting point, not silence.

practice.q: Which instruction should stay exact, with no room for judgement?

options.text: How to choose which pages to open at 760 and 1440 pixels
options.why: That depends on what changed, so signs and judgement work better than a fixed list.

options.text: The command that checks a Django migration: ./manage.py makemigrations --dry-run --check
options.why: There is one right command and a wrong one costs a lot. That is a narrow bridge: give the exact command.

options.text: How deeply to review a CSS-only change
options.why: Depth depends on the change. A goal and signs to look deeper fit better than a fixed rule.

practice.q: Finish the line in the verify skill so the reader knows why the cheap path is closed.
practice.before: Fix the code rather than the check, because
answers: a loosened check hides the next bug too
a loosened check hides the next bug
a weakened check hides the next bug too
a weakened check hides the next bug
practice.hint: What does a weaker check do to the bugs that come after yours?
practice.why: With the reason, the agent can also refuse the variations nobody listed: skipping the test, marking it flaky, or lowering a threshold.

practice.q: A skill says: "Until the end of November, run the old schema check, because the new one is not merged yet." What is wrong with it?

options.why: The reason is fine, but the sentence becomes false on 1 December and nobody will notice.

options.text: It ties the instruction to a date; say what to check ("use npm run verify if it exists, otherwise lint and types") so it stays true
options.why: Text that depends on a date goes stale silently. Describe the condition instead of the calendar.
Short is good. The problem is that it will become wrong.

practice.q: Put the monthly rule diet for one skill in order.
items: The skill's owner picks one rule or section that may no longer earn its place
They open a pull request that removes it
Plugin CI runs the skill's evals with and without the plugin
The scores hold, so the removal is kept
The result goes into the monthly run review
practice.why: Rules pile up. Removing one at a time and keeping the removal only when the evals hold keeps a skill short without guessing.
